title: Localization comparisons for the ringed projection mate
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $R_Y$ be a sheaf of commutative rings and fix an identification $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and derived tensor computed by K-flat total complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For an object $V\to Y$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $U=X\times_YV$ and let $f_V$ be the induced morphism from the localized topos of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ at $U$ to that of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ at $V$. Write $j_V^*$ and $j_U^*$ for restriction to these localized sites and restrict the coefficient sheaves there. For $E\in D(R_X)$ and $P,M,N\in D(R_Y)$ there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$j_V^*Rf_*E\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*E,\qquad j_U^*Lf^*P\cong Lf_V^*j_V^*P,\qquad j_V^*(M\otimes^L N)\cong j_V^*M\otimes^L j_V^*N.$$
Under these isomorphisms, restriction of the adjoint-of-counit projection map for $(f,E,P)$ is exactly the adjoint-of-counit projection map for $(f_V,j_U^*E,j_V^*P)$, including the canonical shift comparisons. A morphism in $D(R_Y)$ is an isomorphism if, for every site object $V$, some covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ makes all its restrictions to $V_i$ isomorphisms. No quasi-compactness or uniform cohomological bound is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] to $u_f(V)=X\times_YV$ from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. This gives the ringed localization square and the restricted coefficient identification. By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], both restrictions are exact, hence their termwise functors are their derived functors [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] to this small ringed-site morphism. Its two canonical comparisons $\beta,\theta$ give the required pushforward and pullback isomorphisms, and their compatibility with the derived units and counits makes $\beta$ the exchange mate of $\theta$ under the defining adjunction bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-pullback-mate-normalization], this $\theta$ is the derived comparison of the ordinary localization square of Step 1: on every flat-term K-flat representative it is the localization of that termwise module square. Hence $\beta$ is the exchange mate of the pullback comparison induced by the commutative ringed square of Step 1, not merely some isomorphism between the same functors.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $j_V$ and $j_U$. Their coefficient maps are identities and their pullbacks are exact restrictions by Step 1, so its comparison is precisely the asserted restriction/tensor isomorphism. [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-comparisons-shift] supplies the shift normalization of these and the two comparisons of Step 2.

In [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] set $g=j_V$, $g'=j_U$, $f'=f_V$ and $Q=P$. Step 1 supplies its ringed square; by Step 2 its pullback comparison induced by that square is the $\theta$ of the slice theorem, so its exchange mate is $\beta$; Step 3 supplies its canonical tensor comparisons. Its equality is the required equality of restricted projection maps. The comparisons commute with shifts by Step 3, and the projection maps do so by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]; thus this equality includes the canonical shift comparisons.

For the last assertion, exact restriction commutes naturally with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]; the same equality on derived arrows follows by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Thus every $H^q(a)$ is invertible on the assumed covering slices. Collect all their domains as a small family; its sieve covers every object. Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] to the underlying abelian sheaves. The inverse is module-linear since $H^q(a)$ is module-linear and bijective. Now [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] makes $a$ invertible. This uses each integer $q$ separately, with no bound or finiteness hypothesis.

Step 1 (localize-ringed-site-morphism with u_f(V)=X×_YV, exact restriction, termwise derived functors) is correct. Step 3 (tensor-pullback applied to j_V and j_U with identity coefficients, Lj^*=j^*) is correct. Step 5 is correct: the domains of the coverings form a small family whose sieve covers every V, so Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop applies to the underlying abelian H^q(a); the inverse is linear, and the unbounded cohomology criterion finishes it with no boundedness hypothesis. Gap fixed (C3/E5): in lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization, β is fixed by the right-derived unit square and θ is defined as its inverse mate (proof, ofMate). Its statement never ties θ to the ordinary localization square. Step 2's sentence 'counit compatibility makes β the mate of θ' is therefore a tautology. Step 4 needs θ to be the pullback comparison induced by the ringed commutation isomorphism, normalized on flat-term K-flat complexes as def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-square-presentation and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-square-tensor-compatibility require. That argument was the old Step 5, which the re-split dropped, and no cited statement supplies it. I checked its sign convention against def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves: the A[n]⊗B map is the identity and the A⊗B[n] map is (-1)^{np}, and both differential parts commute for all n and p, so the statement is true. Its tensor clause overlaps the μ-shift clause of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact for f=j_V; this is advisory only, since that node's 'presented by small ringed sites' hypothesis is unclear for localizations of general sites.
